problem: Structured 3D scene memories (scene graphs) are built before the task is known, so they often omit objects, relations and attributes that later questions need. Over-provisioning or task-specific offline enhancement pipelines are costly and cannot recover information that was never detected.
motivation: Static scene graphs perform poorly on OpenEQA because compression choices are fixed in advance. The authors hypothesize that letting the reasoning VLM edit its own memory at inference time, through targeted perception on keyframes, gives task-conditioned memory without rescanning or extra training.
key_idea: Give the reasoning VLM language-callable APIs (find_objects, analyze_objects, analyze_frame) to query keyframes and write new nodes, edges and notes into a mutable scene graph, navigation log and scratchpad during inference.
insight: Ablation on a 184-question subset shows that the Navigation Log, a structured index of frame contents, gives the largest single gain (+9.6 pp over frames only). The static scene graph adds little (+1.7 pp), and the frame-level API adds another 3.6 pp over the static SG+log setup (46.9 to 50.5). Deeper search helps (46.9 at m=0 to 51.2 at m=20), but shallow search can hurt, likely because partial updates inject misleading info. Gains concentrate in attribute recognition, while spatial and localization questions do slightly worse than image-only.
method: Structured Scene Memory: four linked stores: scene graph (object tracks with point cloud, CLIP and BGE embeddings, caption, room ID, keyframe list), graphical scratchpad with per-node notes, frame memory of n_img evenly spaced keyframes, and navigation log (room, FOV tag, motion label, visible node IDs).

Initial construction: a VLM detector gives boxes and captions, SAM gives masks, depth back-projection with 0.02 m voxel downsampling and DBSCAN cleaning. Tracks are associated by a 3-way vote (CLIP sim>0.7, caption sim>0.8, point overlap>0.4 within 5 cm) needing at least 2 votes, with EMA embedding update.

Edge discovery and consolidation: every 3 frames the VLM predicts four relation types (on top of, subpart of, contained in, attached to) with justifications; captions are periodically summarized by the VLM; rooms and floors follow the HOV-SG pipeline.

Modifiability APIs: find_objects adds query-relevant new detections and notes; analyze_objects writes query-specific notes on listed visible nodes and falls back to find_objects if they are not visible; analyze_frame does both jointly. Each returns a JSON patch merged into the SSM.

Agentic reasoning loop: the VLM reads the serialized SSM (JSON plus interleaved images), iteratively chooses API, frame and natural-language query up to m calls, and must cite both visual (frame) and semantic (scratchpad) evidence in its final answer.

setting.backbone: Gemini 2.0 Flash (frozen; reasoning agent and detector), plus SAM, CLIP ViT-L/14, BGE
setting.observation: sparse RGB-D keyframes with camera poses from pre-recorded scans (episodic memory)
setting.action_space: no physical actions; language API calls (find_objects / analyze_objects / analyze_frame) that edit memory
setting.simulator: none (OpenEQA episodic-memory scans from HM3D and ScanNet)
setting.privileged: none (given camera poses and depth of recorded scan, per EM-EQA protocol)

numbers.extra: n_img=5 initial frames, search depth m=20, frame-level API; baseline image-only Gemini uses 25 frames
numbers.evidence: Table 1 OpenEQA performance comparison, row 9 GraphPad (w/ Gemini 2.0 Flash) 55.3

numbers.method: GraphPad ablation: Frame Memory + SG + Navigation Log + Frame-level API
numbers.extra: 4 initial frames; m=20 gives 51.2 in search depth table; 6 initial frames gives 50.5
numbers.evidence: Table 2 ablation of system components, frame-level API 50.5

numbers_note: Split name is not stated in the paper; 'test' is used as a placeholder for the OpenEQA EM-EQA evaluation. Metric is LLM-judged accuracy, which is not among the canonical keys.
results: GraphPad with Gemini 2.0 Flash reaches 55.3% on OpenEQA EM-EQA, +3.0 pp over the image-only Gemini 2.0 Flash baseline (52.3%) with 5 frames instead of 25. It matches GPT-4V (55.3) and beats static scene-graph baselines (CG 36.5, SVM 38.9) but trails 3D-Mem with GPT-4V (57.2).
limitations: No verification of VLM detections, so errors propagate into the graph; each API call costs a full VLM pass (2-3 s).
API set is minimal and not shown to be optimal; only tested on static-scene QA in medium-sized homes, not on navigation or manipulation.
Underperforms the image-only baseline on spatial understanding, object recognition and localization.
